the_prior_question_answered_yes.and_it_corrects_my_own_school_round: school's counter-finding (c) was too pessimistic. 'he has thumbed zero' is true of the 127 garments; it is NOT true of the repo's history. a rota can ride on something that has worked 39 times.

attempt_1_keyword_matching_ABANDONED.the_miss_that_mattered: BB-BATTERIES-ARE-THE-MONEY came back UNSEEN because there is NO quote of his containing both 'batteries' and 'money'. CLAUDE.md's 'Batteries are the money' is a SUMMARY, not his words, and the precision-first bar correctly refused it.
attempt_1_keyword_matching_ABANDONED.the_finding: THE BOARD'S ROWS AND HIS RULINGS DO NOT SHARE A VOCABULARY. rows are named after mechanics; he talks about intent. a keyword matcher delivers near-zero true positives and a handful of false ones, and a false SEEN hides an item forever.

attempt_2_exact_citation.method: a row built off a ruling of his usually QUOTES HIM in its own text; exact, no guessing
attempt_2_exact_citation.so: so low it demanded its own explanation, and that is where the real finding came from

the_mechanism.why: the citation is present while the work is in flight and gone once it lands, because a SHIPPED line is rewritten to say what the work achieved, with proof paths, and the ruling that caused it is not part of that sentence
the_mechanism.the_one_field_fix: keep the ruling citation on the row when it ships. coverage becomes computable forever, by anybody, in one grep. exactly what school's first finding said: real trackers make this a STATUS and our board has no field for it.

the_matrix.what_it_does_NOT_support: the sentence 'he has never seen these 201 things'. it supports the narrower true claim: NOTHING ON THE BOARD RECORDS THAT HE RULED ON THEM. those are different statements.

rule_zero.and_one_FAILED_on_the_first_run: 'a thing he demonstrably ruled on is findable in the corpus (the UI at 50%)' -- FAIL, and it caught a real bug
rule_zero.the_bug: the harvester matched quotes across the whole file, so ONE unbalanced quote mark put every later pairing off by one; the harvest came back with sentences glued to board rows, one 'quote' ending in '- SHIPPED 9/7 8a13045'
rule_zero.the_fix: a quote may not cross a newline, so each line pairs its own marks; multi-line verbatim blocks in verdict records are captured separately. the corpus went from 690 garbled strings to 341 real quoted rulings.
rule_zero.without_it: I would have published a matrix built on nonsense and it would have looked fine

the_gate.name: SEEN BY HIM
the_gate.holds: ONE number: the citation gap, frozen at 22 points, may only shrink
the_gate.why_the_gap_and_not_a_count: new rows arrive honestly and would push any absolute number around; the gap is immune to growth because both halves move together when the board gets bigger. same lesson as the NO READER gate, where a byte-exact check went red for the whole fleet inside a minute.

routed: NOTHING. the board records what it was designed to record; what it was never designed to record is the link, and that is a board change, not a lane's defect.
blind_spots: the board is not the game: a SHIPPED line is a claim, and E11 and E13 both found shipped claims that were not true on the surface
'no ruling on record' is NOT 'he has never seen it': his rulings from before the board existed live in transcripts nobody kept
the matrix grades 205 rows while the gate counts 210: the matrix needs a two-word label or a NAME-IN-CAPS to grade a row, and five have neither
the risk column is a keyword guess at 'first minute', a heuristic for ordering one item per round, not a claim about importance
nothing here measures whether he would LIKE any of it
